summary: Backend-only testing for iteration 3: BPM + musical key analysis (librosa), Camelot wheel mapping, Discogs tier-3 artwork fallback, and new /admin/mixes/{id}/analyze + /mixes/{id}/analysis_status endpoints. Created /app/backend/tests/test_analysis.py with 9 tests - all passed. Full regression: 41/41 tests green (iter1: 24 + iter2: 8 + iter3: 9).
critical_code_review_comments: audio_analysis.read_audio_info uses m.mime[0] without None-check on the list; if mutagen returns empty mime, IndexError would escape. Low risk because mutagen always returns a non-empty list for supported files, but defensive [0] guard recommended.

_schedule_analysis stores tasks in a module-level _analysis_locks dict with no bounded concurrency. A scan of 100 files will fire 100 concurrent librosa jobs each consuming CPU/RAM (each librosa.load + chroma for ~45s window). Consider a semaphore or asyncio.Queue worker with e.g. 2-4 concurrent workers to prevent thrashing.

server.py is now 990+ lines with DB models, routes, CUE parser, artwork lookups, audio analysis plumbing all together. Recommend splitting into routers/models.py, routers/admin.py, routers/artwork.py, services/analysis.py.

Background analysis errors are only logged via logging.exception - no retry, no visible failure reason in the API response beyond analysis_status='failed'. Consider surfacing last_error string on Mix so the admin UI can show why analysis failed.

GET /mixes/{id}/analysis_status mixes a projection dict ({"_id":0, 'analysis_status':1, 'bpm':1, 'key':1, 'camelot':1}) - MongoDB requires all-inclusion or all-exclusion EXCEPT for _id. This works but is brittle; older Mongo versions warn. Safer to just fetch full doc and pick fields.
_run_mix_analysis writes tracks = analyzed + tracks[i + 1:] as a mid-run checkpoint but then overwrites with final `analyzed` at the end. Works, just extra write.

_lookup_discogs: when DISCOGS_TOKEN is empty the function returns None instantly (good), but when set it uses token= query param. Discogs prefers `Authorization: Discogs token=...` header for tighter rate-limit tiers. Cosmetic.

Artwork cache write happens even on a None/miss, which is good (avoids repeated failed lookups), BUT this means if DISCOGS_TOKEN is later added, already-cached misses won't re-query unless refresh=1 is passed. Document this to the operator.

Track model uses Optional[int] for bpm and Optional[str] for camelot - no validation that camelot matches the {1-12}{A|B} regex. If a buggy analyzer writes '13C' it would be stored. Consider @field_validator or regex Literal type.
seed_data_creation: Created /tmp/mixdeck_analyze_test/ with real_audio.mp3 (copied from /tmp/real_audio.mp3, ~900KB, ~38s) and a 2-track cue (00:00 + 00:18). Cleaned up both DB records via /api/admin/mixes DELETE and the directory after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 complete. Verified: (1) POST /admin/mixes/{id}/analyze 401 without token, (2) GET /mixes/{id}/analysis_status 404 for unknown id, (3) scan with analyze=false -> analysis_queued=0 and status stays 'none', (4) scan with analyze=true (default) -> analysis_queued=added_count, background librosa pipeline completes within ~10s for 2-track 38s mp3 and sets analysis_status='done', track[0].bpm is positive int, track[0].key is non-empty string, track[0].camelot matches ^\d{1,2}[AB]$, (5) re-scanning same directory -> added_count=0, skipped_count=N, analysis_queued=0 (no re-queue for already-ingested mixes), (6) direct /admin/mixes/{id}/analyze returns {ok:true, status:'pending'|'already_running'} and 404 for unknown, (7) /api/tracks/artwork with empty DISCOGS_TOKEN does NOT crash - iTunes-resolvable track returns source='itunes' with valid url, cached=false on refresh=1; fully unknown track returns 200 with source=null without error. All iter1+iter2 regression still green.
rca of the issue: No issues found during iteration 3 testing. End-to-end librosa analysis pipeline verified working in the container environment.
